title: Grateful Dead Live at Roscoe Maples Pavilion - Stanford University on 1973-02-09

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture of Stanford’s historic Feb 9 1973 show, featuring smoking first‑time renditions of They Love Each Other, Loose Lucy and a monster Eyes of the World.
ai_review.review: The Ashley‑produced sbd tape delivers an unusually crisp and balanced mix that lets every instrument shine – even the kick drum is startlingly clear. Musically the concert is a landmark, packed with first‑time performances (They Love Each Other, Loose Lucy, Here Comes Sunshine, Row Jimmy, Wave That Flag) and a monster 18‑minute Eyes of the World, all delivered with high energy and historic excitement.

ai_rating.rationale: The vast majority of reviews rate the show 4–5 stars and praise both performance and sound quality; only one outlier gave a zero rating unrelated to the music, yielding an overall average of ~4.6 which translates to a strong combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Consistently described as crisp, clear and well‑balanced; excellent headphone mix, very good instrument separation, kick drum audible. A few reviewers mistakenly called it “non‑soundboard” but the consensus is that the sbd source is top‑notch.

poor_songs: Off‑key backup vocals on Eyes of the World and China Doll
show_quality.setlist_flow: Historic first‑time material dominates the set, making the first half feel like a warm‑up while the second set erupts with tight jams and groundbreaking arrangements.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia's tone repeatedly called “prime”, “awesome” and “fattened Strat sound”; his solos noted as inverted and superb.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob Weir’s counter‑rhythm praised as never better; his rhythm work highlighted throughout.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s kick drum is especially clear and punchy; overall drumming described as solid.
